title: Keep everything private — local-only and database encryption
description: Reassure on privacy and show the optional database-encryption feature. Recap the Local-only shield on Home, then Settings -> Advanced -> Database encryption: what it does, the one-time recovery code, and the trade-off. A CONCEPTUAL TOUR — the 'Turn on encryption' ceremony is NOT triggered (it would migrate the real demo DB and show a genuine recovery code), so the button is hovered and the recovery-code disclosure is expanded and read, but no real code is shown and nothing is encrypted on camera. Selectors: .rail-foot[data-help-key=local-only]; .tab[data-tab=advanced]; #dbenc-section, #dbenc-section summary, #dbenc-status, #dbenc-encrypt.

steps.narration: ScanFinder runs entirely on this PC. There's no cloud, no online account for your documents — everything stays with you.
steps.caption: Private by design — 100% offline

steps.narration: This little shield, Local only, is your reminder: nothing you scan or file is ever sent anywhere.
steps.caption: The Local-only shield

steps.narration: For an extra layer, open Settings.
steps.caption: 1. Open Settings

steps.narration: and go to the Advanced tab.
steps.caption: 2. Advanced tab

steps.narration: Database encryption locks the file that holds everything ScanFinder has read — so even if that file were copied off your PC, its contents couldn't be read.
steps.caption: Lock the database file

steps.narration: When you turn it on, you're shown a one-time recovery code. That code is the key. Day to day the app just opens; you only need the code if you move to a new PC or restore a backup.
steps.caption: The recovery code is the key

steps.narration: So if you use it, write that code down and keep it somewhere safe — there is no way back into the data without it, not even for us.
steps.caption: Keep the code safe — there's no other way in

steps.narration: Local by default, and lockable when you want it. Your documents stay yours.
steps.caption: Your documents stay yours
